subject.title: [Feature]: Lightweight subagent instruction files (à la Claude Code .claude/agents/)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class `sessions_spawn(label=...)` role-profile file contract, and what prompt authority, model/tool frontmatter, memory/writeback, precedence, and audit semantics should it have?
rationale: This would create a new trusted, model-facing role/config surface that can affect tool policy, provider routing, session context, and security auditability, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped Core Contract
options.body: Add label-backed role files with explicit spawn arguments winning, role files narrowing rather than expanding capabilities, bounded model/provider overrides, docs, tests, and loaded-file audit metadata.

options.title: Route Prompt-Only Roles To Plugins
options.body: Document a plugin or ClawHub pattern for prompt-only role context and leave model/tool frontmatter or memory/writeback out of core until a missing plugin API is proven.

options.title: Keep Existing Surfaces
options.body: Reject first-class role files for now and keep full `agents.list`, explicit `task` instructions, and attachments as the supported mechanisms.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Core Contract
recommendation.body: Add label-backed role files with explicit spawn arguments winning, role files narrowing rather than expanding capabilities, bounded model/provider overrides, docs, tests, and loaded-file audit metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current history across the original `sessions_spawn` API, cross-agent behavior, and subagent bootstrap boundary.
